title: Sepiapterin
overview: Sepiapterin is used to treat hyperphenylalaninemia (HPA; elevated levels of the amino acid phenylalanine) due to phenylketonuria (PKU; disorder where body cannot break down phenylalanine). Sepiapterin is in a class of medications called phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) activators. It works by helping the phenylalanine hydroxylase enzyme to break down phenylalanine to tyrosine.

sections.Before taking sepiapterin,: tell your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, any part of this medication, or any other medications, foods or substances. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about the allergy and what symptoms you had.some medications should not be taken with sepiapterin. Other medications may cause dosing changes or extra monitoring when taken with sepiapterin. Make sure you have discussed any medications you are currently taking or plan to take before starting sepiapterin with your doctor and pharmacist. Before starting, stopping, or changing any medications while taking sepiapterin, please get the advice of your doctor or pharmacist. tell your doctor if you have or have ever had a bleeding disorder or increased risk of bleeding, seizure disorder, or Parkinson's Disease.tell your doctor if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or are breast-feeding. If you become pregnant while taking sepiapterin, call your doctor.if you are having surgery, including dental surgery, tell the doctor or dentist that you are taking sepiapterin.
sections.Sepiapterin may cause side effects. Tell: diarrheaheadachesstomach painorange-colored stoolmouth or throat pain
sections.Some side effects can be serious. If you: unusual bruising, bleeding from gums or prolonged bleeding from cuts or wounds, or heavy menstrual bleedingseizures or convulsions, irritabilitySeptiapterin may cause other side effects. Call your doctor if you have any unusual problems while taking this medication.If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may send a report to the Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online (https://www.fda.gov/Safety/MedWatch) or by phone (1-800-332-1088).
